diffuseAlbedo.note: Purbeck marble, Dorset: a grey-brown limestone packed with pale freshwater snail shells; no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material (as the Oxford University Museum's shafts show it).

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.note: A first open porosity for the rock type; no measurement of this stone was read.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows at gallery distance.

bed.source: Dorset Building Stone, 'Upper Purbeck (Purbeck Marble)': the thin beds are 'usually of less than 12" (.3 m) in thickness but rarely as much as 1.00 m or more'; maximum thicknesses: Blue bed 0.11 m, Green bed 0.81 m, Grey bed 0.38 m, Pre-Unio grey bed 0.20 m; the Green bed 'not uncommonly' oxidises to red. https://www.dorsetbuildingstone.org/upper-purbeck-purbeck-marble.html . Wikipedia, 'Purbeck Marble': beds 'never more than 1.2 m thick and are often much thinner'. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purbeck_Marble
bed.note: Checked. Clarified: 0.3 m is the usual upper limit ('usually of less than 12 in'), not a typical thickness. Most beds are thinner, so 300 mm is the top of the usual range. The per-bed figures are maxima. Neither cited page says that shafts were cut from single beds, so that remains an inference. The Green bed (up to 810 mm, and it can oxidise red) is the exception if a shaft is read as that bed.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
